answer: Weight rewards by unbroken tenure. A key's share starts tiny and grows with the square root of consecutive epochs in which it answered originally, capped after about a year. A farm that spins up 1,000 keys before a payout gets an ocean of names but barely a drop of nectar; to profit it must keep every key writing distinct, passing answers for months, each history cross-checked for overlap. One missed epoch resets the clock, so a long clean record becomes onyx-hard evidence of a real operator.
